title: Audubon · Pine Siskin & Sora
description: Five individually traced birds from public-domain original plates: two Pine Siskins and three Soras.
attribution: John James Audubon, The Birds of America; University of Pittsburgh scans via Wikimedia Commons. Individual source links retained.

assets.title: Audubon · Pine Siskin · Female · head-down feeding
assets.creator: John James Audubon
assets.source_caption: Pine Finch. Fringilla pinus. Male, 1. Female, 2. Pinus pendula, Black-Larch.
assets.attribution: John James Audubon, The Birds of America, plate 180; scan credited to University of Pittsburgh via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
assets.changes: FederFunk: manually traced alpha contour, tight bounding crop, and proportional resize to at most 1400 pixels. Original source pigment and orientation retained; no painting, generative fill, reconstructed anatomy, recoloring or white-key removal. Original occlusions remain. processing.method: Source-pixel alpha contour, bounding crop and proportional resize only

review.species_check: Spinus pinus; Printed 2 immediately left of the upper bird; source caption identifies female 2.
review.orientation: Head down, bill toward lower left, tail toward upper right. Preserve the original feeding pose.
review.crop: Both open bill edges, raised wing tips and separate tail tips preserved. The actual curled foot and gripped cone remain; lower paper/twig wedge trimmed and visible gap below claw made transparent.
review.limitation: Original head-down feeding pose; the cone held by the foot is retained. Hidden anatomy is not reconstructed.
review.scope: Individually compared full prepared RGBA on paper and neutral backgrounds against the original plate, with independent visual review of visible anatomy, silhouette, orientation and retained objects. Labels describe the historical figure, not sex or age inferred from detections.

review.notes: Body and visible curled foot included; gripped cone interior excluded. Geometry viewed as a red exclusion overlay against the actual PNG. Dark contact pigment immediately around toes is retained conservatively.
review.limitation: Visible original bird area, with fine feather and toe edges approximated by reviewed polygons; not a biological body-area measurement.

review.species_check: Porzana carolina; Printed 2 above the left bird's back; caption identifies female 2.
review.orientation: Horizontal body, head facing left, raised tail to the right; feet stand on the original log.
review.crop: Complete visible bill, head, raised tail, body and fine toes traced. Rear feathers end at the original overlap with the central male; the neighbouring bird and background log are omitted.
review.limitation: The rear wing edge is partly hidden by the male in the original plate; that natural occlusion remains.
review.scope: Individually compared full prepared RGBA on paper and neutral backgrounds against the original plate, with independent visual review of visible anatomy, silhouette, orientation and retained objects. Labels describe the historical figure, not sex or age inferred from detections.

review.notes: Visible bird silhouette, including both legs and all visible toes. Background log and reeds omitted from the cutout; original occlusions and small ambiguous source-colored edge remnants retained.
review.limitation: Visible original bird area, with fine feather and toe edges approximated by reviewed polygons; not a biological body-area measurement.
